summary:
Continued the D25 thumb refit from run 8's checkpoint (poses/s8/fA.ckpt.json). I checked it in Blender (R19): every gate passed. I then ran 8 more LM iterations with fit7, the D25-constrained fit (fA2: cost 589 -> 537). After that I slid the thumb IP 8 px along MCP->tip onto its reading. That fixes the thumb phalanx proportions: 3D P1/P2 goes from 0.90 to 1.14, and the drawn keypoints give 1.12. Last, two radius touch-ups for taper (thumb_ip r 27.0, ring_dip r 17.45). The installed pose is outputs/qa/scratch/calib-left/poses/s9/final9.pose-left.json, with its notes rewritten.

What changed in the thumb:
- thumb_cmc moved from 42.8 px (2.86 u) off its reading (430,330) to 12.3 px (0.82 u).
- The metacarpal now leaves the base of the palm toward the camera.
- MCP sideways bend 24.8 -> 10.9 deg; IP sideways -7.9 -> -4.6 deg. Both are inside D25's bounds (about 12 / 5).
- The MCP flexion of 37 deg lies in depth, so the phalanges run nearly parallel to the image plane.
- The tip moved 7.6 px back along IP->tip, about 2 px short of the verifier's e7 point. Putting it exactly on e7 pushes the IP sideways bend to -5.8 deg. The rendered thumb end matches e7's (d25-thumb-end-6x.png).
- The thenar (0.90), palm heel, wrist crease (35.3 px) and thumb_root_cap (3.86) were refitted to the palm-heel outline.
- thumb_roll_deg stays 95 (D24). The nail is now 8.1 deg off the camera instead of 3.0, because the thumb frame follows the new metacarpal direction. It still faces the viewer.

Groove: the long groove on the back of the hand (the verifier's minor) is gone. A short soft fold remains at the first web, where the thenar, the web and the index metacarpal meet.

I tried one extra fit (fC) that held the thumb MCP near its reading (478,372). The silhouette pulled the MCP sideways bend straight back to the bound (11.1 deg) and gave a worse P1/P2 (1.03), so I dropped it.

Final repo build R22, with --views: IoU 0.98363, contour mean 0.776, p95 2.000 (109 of 213 allowed edge px over 2), negative-space IoU 0.93267. Every tip and all 16 joints pass. A1 and D9 pass.
anatomy:
Thumb chain, in the builder's own thumb frame (tools8/thumbang.py, the verifier's decomposition). Committed -> final:
- MCP flexion -0.9 -> 37.1 deg; MCP sideways 24.8 -> 10.9 deg.
- IP flexion 27.2 -> 6.6 deg; IP sideways -7.9 -> -4.6 deg.
- Nail 3.0 -> 8.1 deg off the camera.
- 2D segment angles 26.4/53.6/46.5 -> 32.7/51.7/47.8 deg. The keypoint chain gives 41.2/46.3/45.0.
- Thumb metacarpal 3D 25-50 deg from the hand axis (a fit constraint).
- The 2D bend that remains at the MCP comes from the MCP flexion in depth, not from a sideways bend.
- Pulling the MCP 25/50 % toward its reading (478,372) straightens the sideways bend to 6.4/2.3 deg in the surrogate. But the edge px over 2 rise to 179/247 of 213, and refitting (fC) returned the MCP to 11.1 deg sideways.

Bone lengths, projected / 3D (ref px at z 0), committed -> final:
- Thumb metacarpal 93.6/99.1 -> 60.7/91.2. It now points toward the camera; 3D -8 %.
- Thumb P1 66.0/70.7 -> 75.1/74.0.
- Thumb P2 82.9/78.7 -> 67.5/64.8. P2 was too long before (the verifier's minor).
- Thumb 3D P1/P2 0.90 -> 1.14; the drawn keypoints give 1.12.
- Index 106.9/104.3, 80.3/78.9, 53.6/52.3: unchanged.
- Middle 73.7/75.5, 59.8/62.2, 69.2/70.8: unchanged. P1/P2 1.21 (D23).
- Ring P1 73.8/76.6 -> 74.6/77.7, P2 52.8/56.1 -> 49.9/53.1, P3 59.7/62.9 -> 61.4/64.6. 3D P1/P2 1.36 -> 1.46. The ring joints were free in the fit; 1.46 is inside D18's original 1.4-1.6.
- Pinky 60.0/64.4 -> 59.0/63.7, 29.9/34.1 -> 30.3/33.6, 24.2/26.8 -> 24.0/26.2.
- Wrist->palm 167.5/164.8 -> 165.5/162.5.

Radii, base -> tip:
- Thumb 32.2 / 27.06 / 27.0 / 19.84.
- Index 33.7 / 21.3 / 16.4 / 12.1.
- Middle 30.2 / 21.7 / 16.9 / 13.6.
- Ring 24.5 / 17.5 / 17.45 / 11.7.
- Pinky 19.2 / 13.7 / 12.0 / 10.1.
- All non-increasing. The thumb IP and MCP, and the ring DIP and PIP, are equal to within 0.06 px.

Hinges (D23):
- Index: abduction -6.1, MCP -1.1, PIP 16.7, DIP -8.9.
- Middle: abduction 4.8, MCP flexion 31.2, PIP 39.3, DIP 15.0.
- Ring: abduction 4.9, MCP flexion 47.6, PIP 38.6, DIP 14.9.
- Pinky: abduction 0.2, MCP 80.5, PIP 54.1, DIP -20.0.
- P2 and P3 are within 0.2 deg of the hinge plane.
- Knuckle line 11.6 deg off the lateral axis; dorsal unchanged [0.324, 0.905, -0.276].

Digit identity is as D2. The thumb is the nail-facing digit from the palm base and sits in front of the ring and pinky; the pinky is the short curled digit. In 3D (capsules), no two segments of different digits come closer than 1.2x the sum of their radii.

Views (R22, left-view-{home,yawp35,yawm35,above}.png; sheet compare-left/d25-views-committed-vs-final-2x.png): volumetric, nothing paper-thin. In the +-35 deg views the thumb comes diagonally out of a rounded thenar instead of lying along the hand axis. From above the loose fist and knuckle bumps are unchanged.

Groove, depth below the convex envelope (tools9/valley.py) along the verifier's line 404,256->416,300:
- valley 23.2 -> 6.4 px; sharpness (second difference) 0.81 -> 0.22.
- The long light groove floor in the home view is gone (d25-groove-home-4x.png).
- What remains is a short soft fold at the first web, around (446-462, 290-300): valley 23.4 px, second difference 1.19. It is where the thenar, the web and the index metacarpal meet; the drawing has converging strokes there.
- Filling it with a larger or lower FDI breaks the dorsal outline (surrogate: 220-317 edge px over 2 against 213 allowed).

openIssues: verify:left#1 major (thumb not straight): fixed within D25's bounds. MCP sideways 24.8 -> 10.9 deg, IP -7.9 -> -4.6 deg, thumb_cmc 2.86u -> 0.82u. The MCP sideways bound is binding: every fit (fA2 and fC) settles at 10.9-11.1 deg, because the silhouette pulls toward more bend. A straighter thumb would need the builder change listed in builderRequests.

verify:left#1 minor (thumb end about 11.5 px long): fixed. The tip moved 7.6 px back along IP->tip and the rendered end matches e7's (d25-thumb-end-6x.png). It is about 2 px short of the exact e7 point; exactly on e7 the IP sideways bend becomes -5.8 deg.

verify:left#1 minor (groove on the back of the hand): the long groove is gone. Along the verifier's line the valley went 23.2 -> 6.4 px and the second difference 0.81 -> 0.22. A short soft fold remains at the first web, around home-view (446-462, 290-300): valley 23.4 px, second difference 1.19. It is faint at 1x and visible at 4-5x (d25-groove-home-4x.png, crops/r9/web-ref-committed-R21-5x.png); in the -35 deg view it reads as a soft dimple (crops/r9/yawm35-pit-R19-R21-5x.png). The FDI mass cannot fill it without breaking the dorsal outline.

The thumbnail is now 8.1 deg off the camera instead of 3.0, with thumb_roll_deg still 95 (D24). The builder takes the thumb frame from the metacarpal direction, and the refit changed that direction. The nail still faces the viewer, and its shape, relief and outline are unchanged.
Ring 3D P1/P2 moved 1.36 -> 1.46 because the ring joints were free in the D25 fit. That is inside D18's original 1.4-1.6; the ring bones changed by at most 5 %. Middle stays 1.21.
The thumb metacarpal's 3D length is 8 % shorter (99.1 -> 91.2). It now points toward the camera, and its projected length went 93.6 -> 60.7.
The index-tip contact gap needs both hands, so the main session checks it. The index tip is unchanged (silhouette tip 2.24 px from its reference).
builderRequests: (Optional, recorded per D25's option C, although p95 passed.) Place and orient the thenar and palm heel independently of the thumb metacarpal, and take the thumb frame from the nail rather than from the metacarpal direction. Evidence: with D25's bounds the silhouette pulls the thumb MCP sideways bend to the bound in every fit (fA2: 10.9 deg; fC, with the MCP held near its reading: 11.1 deg; logs outputs/qa/scratch/calib-left/poses/s9/fA2.log and fC.log). Moving the MCP 25/50 % toward its reading (478,372) straightens the bend to 6.4/2.3 deg but costs 179/247 edge px over 2 (213 allowed), because the thenar follows the metacarpal. Separately, the thumbnail's angle to the camera moved 3.0 -> 8.1 deg at the same thumb_roll_deg because the frame follows the metacarpal.

(Minor) Let the first web between the thumb and index metacarpals be filled on its dorsal side without moving the dorsal outline, for example an FDI or web mass that can be placed below the dorsal silhouette line. Evidence: a short soft fold at home-view (446-462, 290-300), valley 23.4 px, second difference 1.19 (tools9/valley.py on public/assets/hand-left.glb, line 455,280->470,320). Enlarging the FDI or lowering its lift breaks the dorsal outline in the surrogate (fdi_size 0.35: 220 of 213 edge px over 2; lift 0-0.3 at size 0.4: 305-317).
